lead.headline: Tokenized equity perps hit $470B monthly volume as infrastructure and regulation converge on institutional rails
lead.tldr: This week marks a pivot from speculative RWA narratives to measurable institutional adoption: tokenized equity derivatives are now generating real volume, Telegram is deploying non-custodial wallets at scale, and the U.S. and Russia are both advancing regulatory frameworks that assume crypto will operate inside existing financial plumbing.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week the gap between crypto-native infrastructure and traditional financial rails narrowed measurably, with volume, regulatory clarity, and institutional balance-sheet moves all pointing in the same direction.

top_signals.title: Tokenized equity perps drive RWA trading boom to $470 billion monthly volume
top_signals.summary: Real World Asset (RWA) trading has experienced a massive surge, reaching $470 billion in monthly volume. This growth is primarily driven by the popularity of tokenized equity perpetuals over tokenized commodities.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $470 billion monthly volume in tokenized equity perps demonstrates that RWA demand is currently skewed toward synthetic exposure rather than physical-backed assets, which has implications for how we underwrite infrastructure plays versus issuance platforms.

top_signals.title: Telegram plans 'largest rollout of a non-custodial crypto wallet in human history'
top_signals.summary: Telegram is planning a massive rollout of a non-custodial crypto wallet to its vast user base. The move is seen as a significant effort to onboard a mainstream audience into the cryptocurrency ecosystem.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Telegram's wallet rollout at 900 million users is a distribution event that could reprice consumer-facing infrastructure on user-acquisition cost models, not technology metrics.

top_signals.title: Trump agrees to ethics provision as crypto bill inches closer to Senate vote
top_signals.summary: President Trump has agreed to include ethics provisions in a pending crypto bill, removing a potential hurdle for its passage. This agreement brings the legislation closer to a Senate vote and potential enactment into law.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Trump's acceptance of ethics provisions removes the last identifiable procedural obstacle to a Senate vote, meaning U.S. crypto legislation now trades on political will rather than legal drafting risk.

top_signals.title: Bitmine expands Ethereum treasury to 5.78 million ETH, repurchases 5.5 million shares
top_signals.summary: Bitmine has significantly increased its Ethereum holdings to 5.78 million ETH. Additionally, the company repurchased 5.5 million shares as part of a larger $4 billion buyback initiative.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Bitmine's accumulation to 5.78 million ETH, paired with a $4 billion buyback, signals that corporate treasury strategy is now a two-sided bet on asset appreciation and equity rerating through Bitcoin-style mechanics.

top_signals.title: Storj files for bankruptcy, explores equity path for tokenholders 20m, Storj files for bankruptcy, explores equity path for tokenholders The decentralized storage provider says its network will continue operating during Chapter 11 as it explores a court-approved ownership mechanism for STORJ holders.
top_signals.summary: Decentralized storage provider Storj has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. The company intends to keep its network operational while exploring a court-approved mechanism to provide equity to STORJ token holders.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Storj's bankruptcy with continued network operation and a token-to-equity conversion mechanism is a template for how decentralized protocols may survive entity-level failure, but it also tests whether token holders will accept equity-like rights without equity-like governance.

top_signals.title: Russia’s Sberbank to launch crypto trading infrastructure this year10m, Russia’s Sberbank to launch crypto trading infrastructure this yearRussia’s biggest bank plans to create cryptocurrency trading infrastructure by Dec. 1 as the country is set to establish rules for market participants while allowing crypto assets to be used in foreign trade operations.
top_signals.summary: Russia's largest bank, Sberbank, intends to launch a cryptocurrency trading infrastructure by December 1. This move aligns with new national rules allowing the use of crypto assets for foreign trade operations.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Sberbank's December 1 deadline for crypto trading infrastructure, tied to foreign trade settlement use cases, means a G20 systemically important bank is now building on the assumption that crypto rails will handle cross-border flows under sanctions-adapted conditions.

deals.summary: World Foundation has secured $52.5 million in a funding round led by Pantera Capital. The capital will be used to further expand and develop the World ID infrastructure.

Mirae Asset has completed the acquisition of Korbit, officially becoming the largest shareholder of the South Korean cryptocurrency exchange. This move signals a significant expansion of a major traditional financial institution into the digital asset market.

MicroStrategy has increased its cash reserves to $3.225 billion by selling MSTR shares, raising $263.5 million. The company continues its aggressive Bitcoin accumulation strategy, now holding 843,775 BTC.

on_the_radar.title: KB Kookmin Bank to Launch JPMorgan Kinexys Cross-Border Payment Service
on_the_radar.summary: KB Kookmin Bank is integrating JPMorgan's Kinexys blockchain platform to facilitate cross-border US dollar settlements. The service will operate across 10 different countries, marking a significant institutional adoption of blockchain for traditional banking payments.

on_the_radar.title: BitMart to Wind Down Exchange as BMX Tanks
on_the_radar.summary: BitMart has announced it will wind down its cryptocurrency exchange operations following reports of user withdrawal delays. Trading is set to halt on August 26, with all platform operations ceasing in January.

on_the_radar.title: EU adds HTX to Russia sanctions list, barring transactions starting Aug. 23
on_the_radar.summary: The European Union has added the crypto exchange HTX and several other platforms to its Russia sanctions list. These entities are barred from conducting transactions starting August 23.

on_the_radar.title: Fidelity Joins Push for Senate Passage of CLARITY Act
on_the_radar.summary: Fidelity has joined industry groups in urging the US Senate to pass the CLARITY Act. The move signals strong institutional support for establishing a clearer regulatory market structure for digital assets in the United States.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin Policy Institute, Palantir and Anduril join US State Department's Freedom Tech Excellence Program
on_the_radar.summary: The Bitcoin Policy Institute has partnered with Palantir and Anduril as part of the U.S. State Department's Freedom Tech Excellence Program. This represents a significant integration of Bitcoin-focused policy and advanced technology firms within U.S. diplomatic and governmental frameworks.

on_the_radar.title: Thailand SEC Files Complaint Against Bitkub Over 2021 Hack Reporting
on_the_radar.summary: The Thailand SEC has filed a complaint against Bitkub and two former directors regarding false disclosures following a 2021 cyberattack. The hack in question resulted in losses totaling approximately $50 million.

on_the_radar.title: Arthur Hayes, BitMEX co-founders face fraud claims over alleged 'Insider Trading Desk' as exchange winds down
on_the_radar.summary: BitMEX co-founders Arthur Hayes, Samuel Reed, and Benjamin Delo are facing a proposed class action lawsuit. The claims allege the existence of an 'insider trading desk' and the intentional freezing of servers to manipulate outcomes.

on_the_radar.title: Samsung Wallet to Add Stablecoin Support
on_the_radar.summary: Samsung is expanding the capabilities of Samsung Wallet by adding support for stablecoins. This move follows the previous integration of cryptocurrency purchasing features via Coinbase.

on_the_radar.title: Hopes for key crypto bill fade amid delays, Trump ethics controversy
on_the_radar.summary: The CLARITY Act, a key piece of cryptocurrency legislation, is facing significant delays and may not pass due to mid-term political pressures. The bill's progress is further complicated by ethics controversies surrounding Donald Trump.

on_the_radar.title: BitMEX hit with 623 BTC lawsuit on day it announces shutdown 7m, BitMEX hit with 623 BTC lawsuit on day it announces shutdown The proposed class action alleges BitMEX used privileged trading access and server freezes to profit from forced liquidations.
on_the_radar.summary: BitMEX is facing a class action lawsuit seeking 623 BTC over allegations of market manipulation and unfair trading practices. The lawsuit claims the exchange used privileged access and server freezes to profit from forced user liquidations.

on_the_radar.title: Coinbase calls AI payments its 'most high-conviction bet' as businesses begin accepting agent payments
on_the_radar.summary: Coinbase is positioning AI payments as a primary growth driver, enabling businesses to accept payments from AI agents. This initiative leverages Coinbase Payments and the x402 standard to facilitate autonomous machine-to-machine transactions.

on_the_radar.title: Coinbase invests in tokenized version of Abu Dhabi’s sovereign wealth fund
on_the_radar.summary: Coinbase is investing in a tokenized version of a private-markets fund managed by Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund, Mubadala. Infrastructure provider KAIO will be responsible for building the necessary architecture to enable this tokenization.

linkedin_post: Telegram is about to push non-custodial wallets to nine hundred million users. That number is the story. Not the technology, not the seed phrase flow, not the TON integration details. Nine hundred million. The largest distribution event in crypto's history, executed by a messaging app that already owns the attention layer. We have spent years underwriting consumer crypto on the assumption that user acquisition costs would collapse when a major platform made the move. This is the move. The question is what gets repriced first: wallet infrastructure valuations, L1 throughput assumptions, or the entire thesis that mainstream users will tolerate self-custody friction. My bet is on the infrastructure layer. Telegram's users will not care about non-custodial architecture. They will care about whether the payment works. If it works, the wallet becomes plumbing. If it fails, the non-custodial narrative takes a hit that lasts years. The testable thesis: measure TON daily active addresses thirty days post-rollout against the first week. Sustained engagement means the distribution hypothesis holds. Drop-off means we overestimated readiness. One other thing. Sberbank's December 1 deadline for crypto trading infrastructure is running in parallel. Russia's largest bank, building for foreign trade settlement. Two massive distribution events. One consumer, one institutional. Both assuming crypto rails are the default, not the experiment. That is not a hedge. That is a convergence.
